writeup: TIC 264099112 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 5.9744 days. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 19.83 percent, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 8.1 sigma significance, occurring at orbital phase -0.38. The automated TESS photometry analysis achieved a strong detection signal of 483.5 using the Box Least Squares method, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 53.4. However, the centroid offset measured 5.4 arcseconds from the target location, which warrants consideration when evaluating the candidate. This object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the machine-learning screening assigned it a likelihood score of 0.71 on a 0-to-1 scale.
